title: Approval lifecycle: MSA/DPA evidence handoff & technical preflight
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked procurement and legal through outstanding MSA/DPA items and technical evidence for security/compliance. Customer emphasized on-prem/VPC constraints for regulated PII, explicit KMS control, and an SLA-backed latency target. Agreement to exchange redlines and run a 2-week pilot with traffic cap; next steps include delivering redlined contracts, security package, and a connectivity diagram.
next_steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA and DPA + security evidence bundle by 2025-09-12
Sparrow to confirm list of systems requiring VPC peering and provide network contacts by 2025-09-15
SE to share pilot runbook and suggested test prompts/benchmarks by 2025-09-11
Legal to review redlines and provide counterpoints by 2025-09-19
Schedule pilot kickoff meeting (2 weeks) — tentative 2025-09-22
action_items: Jordan Blake — Send redlined MSA/DPA + SOC2/ISO snapshot and security package — due 2025-09-12
Priya Rao — Upload pilot runbook and sample benchmark spreadsheet link to drive — due 2025-09-11
Alex Martinez — Share procurement routing and internal approvers list — due 2025-09-15
Maya Torres — Provide list of required encryption/HSM/KMS constraints and self-hosting constraints — due 2025-09-14
Lena Price — Flag any non-starter DPA clauses and provide legal contact for negotiation — due 2025-09-19
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Alex Martinez (Procurement), Lena Price (Legal), Samir Patel (CTO), Maya Torres (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. My name's Jordan Blake — I'm the AE on this account — and with me is Priya Rao, our SE. We're here to walk through the remaining MSA/DPA points and then do a quick technical handoff for the pilot.

[00:12] Alex: Yep, thanks Jordan, Alex here. Really curious to see the security artifacts too. We've got legal and SecOps on the line so want to make sure we don't do two rounds of redlines.

[00:20] Lena: Hi all, Lena from legal. Main asks are around data residency, liability caps, and subprocessors list. We also need clarity on the KMS model — customer-managed keys vs. Redwood-managed.

[00:32] Samir: Samir, CTO. From engineering, latency SLOs and the ability to run within our VPC matter. We'll likely prefer Dedicated or Private deployment if the egress costs and latency are acceptable.

[00:45] Priya: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: 1) contract redline status; 2) security/compliance evidence; 3) deployment/connectivity options; 4) pilot plan and pricing pathway. If anything else, shout out.

[00:58] Jordan: Quick note — we'll surface the redlined MSA and an alternate DPA that narrows identifiables. Also, there's a proposed SLA amendment around latency and rollback windows — we'll cover that.

[01:12] Alex: On SLA: our procurement team needs a 99.9% availability clause for dedicated throughput during business hours and an explicit rollback policy if latency degrades beyond 200ms p95 for two consecutive minutes. Is that something Redwood will accept?

[01:32] Priya: Okay so a couple of things — Redwood's Dedicated offering has SLOs we can back with credits; 99.9% can be discussed for reserved pools. Latency p95 of 200ms is tight depending on model choice and sequence length. For small prompt sizes and when using an optimized quantized variant, that's plausible in Dedicated in region, but we'd want to define model + instance type up front. Also we do automatic fallback — if capacity hits, requests can route to a slightly higher-latency variant.

[01:58] Samir: That fallback is, like, what's the failover behavior? We need deterministic behavior so our app doesn't see bursts of 1s latencies.

[02:08] Priya: Right so we can put an explicit routing policy in the runbook: prefer Dedicated with pinned model vX, fallback to hosted-compatible quantized variant only after N% CPU/GPU saturation and with a max-added-latency cap. We'll document the thresholds.

[02:26] Lena: Back to contracts, on liability cap we normally push to 1x annual fees for SaaS, is that standard? Also, subprocessors list — we need to know if any third-party infra or telemetry vendors are used.

[02:40] Jordan: Our standard is 1x annual fees but we can be flexible depending on the enterprise add-on. Subprocessors: cloud infra partners, monitoring/logging vendors, and a storage provider for cached KV store. We'll provide the full list in the security bundle.

[02:53] Maya: For SecOps: KMS question — can you support customer-managed keys in a VPC/private deployment? We need to ensure that keys never leave our KMS and that Redwood's control plane only holds an envelope key.

[03:06] Priya: Yes — for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS via standard KMS/HSM APIs; envelope encryption is the pattern. For Hosted we offer a customer-managed key option too, but there are caveats around key rotation windows and sequence for disaster recovery. We'll include a diagram.

[03:23] Alex: Egress billing — important. If we route to Hosted fallback during spikes, will egress be billed differently? Procurement needs clarity on billing paths for fallback traffic.

[03:34] Jordan: Good point — we'll include a billing matrix. Fallback to Hosted counts as hosted usage for billing; Dedicated reserved commit covers baseline. We can outline burst credits. We'll also put sample scenarios with token counts so your FinOps can model costs.

[03:50] Samir: On network connectivity — we assume VPC peering plus private link? We have strict ingress filters.

[03:58] Priya: For Private mode we do VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on your cloud. We'll share a connectivity diagram and the specific firewall rules. For Dedicated we can offer private network endpoints too.

[04:12] Lena: Also — data retention and delete APIs. We need confirmation that customer data used for caching or KV stores can be TTL'd and deleted on demand.

[04:23] Priya: Yes, we support TTL and explicit deletion APIs; we'll state retention policies in the DPA and provide the API spec. There may be short-lived replication windows for HA, which we'll document.

[04:35] Jordan: Let's talk timeline — procurement says they want approvals in the next three weeks to hit a Q4 pilot. Is that accurate, Alex?

[04:43] Alex: Realistic timeline is three weeks for initial approvals if contract redlines aren't huge. If legal stalls then it's four to six. We want the pilot to start late September.

[04:53] Priya: Our proposed pilot is 2 weeks, limited to a sample of traffic with a 10k token/day cap, with a replay harness for your tests. We'll run the benchmark sheet against your prompt set and provide latency and cost breakdowns.

[05:07] Samir: For the pilot we want production-like conditions: concurrent requests, burst patterns, and a subset of longer context. Can Redwood simulate that?

[05:16] Priya: Absolutely — we'll run synthetic and real replay tests. We'll need a sample traffic file and some service account creds. We'll give options for on-prem replay versus Redwood-hosted replay.

[05:30] Lena: A couple of redline items: 1) data residency clause to specify EU-only processing for certain datasets; 2) indemnity carveouts for regulated PII; 3) audit rights — can we get quarterly audit evidence?

[05:46] Jordan: For EU processing, we can pin region and offer a Private deployment in an EU region. Indemnity is negotiable — we'll aim to keep standard limits, but we'll escalate if needed. Quarterly audit evidence — we can provide SOC2 Type II and an ISO snapshot and make redacted SOC artifacts available under NDA.

[06:05] Maya: On audit — we also need architecture diagrams showing where telemetry is sent. Some of the redlines we've seen from other vendors hide telemetry endpoints.

[06:13] Priya: We'll include architecture and telemetry endpoints in the security package. We'll also list telemetry toggles and data minimization controls.

[06:25] Jordan: Quick check — are there any absolute blockers right now? Anything that would kill the pilot?

[06:31] Alex: If we can't do customer-managed KMS or pin region for processing, that's a blocker. Also if liability stays uncapped at unlimited.

[06:40] Lena: Agreed. If KMS can't be customer-controlled in Private, we won't sign.

[06:46] Priya: Understood. For Private deployments, KMS customer-managed is supported. We'll provide a tech note that describes the envelope encryption handshake and key rotation limits.

[06:58] Samir: On SLO quantification — can we do a short table that maps model variant to expected p50/p95 in Dedicated at our target instance class? For planning.

[07:08] Priya: Yes — Priya to generate a benchmark sheet mapping model, sequence lengths, instance type, expected p50/p95 and token/sec throughput. It will be empirical but useful.

[07:18] Jordan: We'll post that in the drive link after the call. Also, I'll attach a sample redline so you can see what we're likely to propose.

[07:24] Alex: On pricing: procurement will want a committed reserved capacity with a monthly commit and an option for burst. What commit sizes do you typically accept?

[07:34] Jordan: Typically starts at a 4-week minimum for Dedicated with a commit of 50-100k tokens/day equivalent, but enterprise can customize. We'll propose a 3-month pilot with optional conversion to a reserved plan. We can also discuss a staged commit where you ramp to full capacity over 6 weeks.

[07:50] Lena: Can Redwood provide a buyout or early termination credit if we sign annual and then stop? We need to understand financial exposure.

[07:58] Jordan: We'll include termination language in the MSA draft. There's usually a prorated refund on unused committed capacity with a notice window. We'll mark it in the redline.

[08:08] Maya: A security nuance — for certain regulated PII we require that no logs are stored in third-party logging systems. Can those logs be disabled per tenant?

[08:18] Priya: Yes, per-tenant telemetry controls exist; you can disable or filter logs. For audit we might need limited redacted logs but we'll work with your SecOps on the minimum necessary.

[08:30] Samir: Let's walk the connectivity steps if we do Private: 1) network contact exchange; 2) temporary test accounts; 3) pilot config; 4) go/no-go. How long is the network setup window?

[08:41] Priya: Usually 3-5 business days for VPC peering once firewall rules are agreed; PrivateLink sometimes longer depending on cloud account approvals. We'll make a checklist.

[08:53] Jordan: I'm going to quickly read out the items we'll include in the security bundle so everyone knows: SOC2 Type II redacted report, ISO summary, subcontractor list, architecture diagram, KMS integration note, telemetry controls, data retention APIs, and a sample runbook for the pilot.

[09:08] Lena: Good. On subprocessors, list specifics — don't just say "monitoring vendor". Procurement will need names.

[09:16] Jordan: Agreed. We'll give names and contact points where permissible.

[09:22] Alex: One more on pricing modeling — can you give us example invoices for a month at low, medium, and high traffic? That really helps procurement rationalize.

[09:31] Jordan: We'll produce a cost model spreadsheet with scenarios: pilot (10k tokens/day), moderate (100k tokens/day), and ramp (1M tokens/day). It'll show hosted vs dedicated vs private egress lines.

[09:44] Samir: Also include the perf delta for using int8 quantized variants vs fp16, so we can weigh cost vs latency/quality.

[09:51] Priya: Good call. We'll mark quantization impacts in the benchmark sheet and note any quality regression caveats.

[10:02] Jordan: Lena, legal — what are the top two items you want us to prioritize in the redline?

[10:07] Lena: 1) Data residency carveout; 2) Audit and indemnity clarity. If those are cleaner, procurement moves faster.

[10:13] Jordan: Great. We'll push those first and label them critical.

[10:18] Alex: For the pilot kickoff, who should be the single point of contact from Redwood?

[10:21] Jordan: Jordan will be primary for commercial and scheduling, Priya will run technical. We'll include an escalation chart.

[10:28] Maya: A thing on encryption lifecycle — if we rotate a customer key, what's the failover pattern? We need an ops playbook.

[10:34] Priya: We'll include key rotation playbook — envelope rotation is seamless if the KMS policy allows decrypt for prior keys for a brief window; otherwise we provide a failback procedure.

[10:45] Samir: Ops question — will you allow us to bring our own inference container to run on Dedicated? We have optimized kernels for some models.

[10:54] Priya: For Dedicated there's an option for customer-owned models/containers under a managed-hosting agreement. That path is more involved from security and patching standpoints but doable. We'll flag it as an advanced option.

[11:07] Jordan: We're at about 11 minutes in — quick pulse: do we have any blockers left?

[11:12] Lena: No blockers besides the KMS and the data residency assurances.

[11:16] Alex: Same from procurement. We'll wait for the redlines and the cost scenarios.

[11:20] Jordan: Ok, next we want to confirm the final deliverables and dates. Priya, can you walk through the pilot artifacts?

[11:26] Priya: Sure — pilot artifacts: test harness (replay), sample prompts, perf benchmark sheet, runbook with routing/pinning, rollback policy, connectivity checklist. We'll post links. Here's the sample sheet link: drive.redwood.ai/sparrow/pilot-bench-2025 (note: placeholder).

[11:44] Samir: Clarify the rollback policy: if p95 > 500ms for X minutes, we automatically route to fallback and then operator review? We want a human-in-loop step for major changes.

[11:56] Priya: We can do an auto-fallback with immediate notifications and human approval to persist fallback. We'll include thresholds and an operator runbook.

[12:05] Jordan: Great. Anything else on the DPA side before we wrap?

[12:10] Lena: One last ask: breach notification timing — legal typically requires 72 hours maximum, but for joint operations we ask for immediate notification and a 24-hr initial alert. Can Redwood meet that?

[12:22] Jordan: We commit to 24-hour initial notification for confirmed incidents and full report within 72. We'll put that into the DPA.

[12:31] Alex: Sounds good. Procurement will wait for the cost model and redlines.

[12:36] Jordan: We'll aim to get the redlined MSA/DPA and pack sent by end of the day Friday (2025-09-12). Priya will upload the pilot runbook tomorrow.

[12:46] Maya: Is there anything we need to provide immediately to unblock the security package?

[12:50] Lena: The list of regulated datasets and the systems needing VPC peering.

[12:55] Alex: Also send the contact for the billing/finops reviewer.

[13:02] Jordan: Noted. I'll include all requested contact points in the email.

[13:08] Priya: I'll follow up with the benchmark template and a short questionnaire for the traffic sample.

[13:16] Samir: For the pilot, we'll prepare a traffic file and point to a staging environment. Expect a security review of the test accounts.

[13:26] Jordan: Ok, quick recap for minutes: Redwood sends redlines+security bundle by 2025-09-12; SE sends pilot runbook by 2025-09-11; Sparrow sends network contacts and dataset classification by 2025-09-15; legal to respond with redlines by 2025-09-19. Pilot kickoff tentative 2025-09-22.

[13:46] Lena: That matches our notes. We'll schedule legal review internally.

[13:50] Alex: Thanks folks, appreciate the clarity.

[13:53] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the drive link and redline packet. End call.

[56:50] (call ended)
additional_notes: Shared artifacts: redline sample (link in follow-up), pilot benchmark spreadsheet (drive link placeholder), security package (SOC2/ISO snapshots)
Legal expressed urgency on KMS and data residency as gating items
Procurement wants explicit billing scenarios and sample invoices
